datasources.title: Data sources
datasources.lead: Connections to the databases and services that Kalzit queries.
datasources.empty.title: No data sources yet
datasources.empty.text: Add a data source to query it in Explore and in dashboards. PostgreSQL, MySQL and MariaDB, SQL Server, SQLite and Prometheus are available.
datasources.empty.textReadOnly: Here are the data sources your role or access given to you lets you use. An admin adds them and gives access.
datasources.noOrg.title: No organization
datasources.noOrg.text: Data sources belong to an organization. Ask an admin to add you to one.
datasources.forbidden.title: No access
datasources.forbidden.text: Your role cannot see data sources. Dashboards shared with you still show their data.
datasources.forbidden.textWrite: Only admins add and change data sources.
datasources.deleted: The data source moved to the trash. Dashboards that use it show an error until you restore it.
datasources.column.name: Name
datasources.new.title: Add data source
datasources.new.lead: Choose the kind of database or service, then enter how Kalzit reaches it.
datasources.edit.title: Data source
datasources.readOnly.lead: Use a database login that can only read. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.form.name: Name
datasources.form.nameRequired: Enter a name for the data source.
datasources.form.number: Enter a whole number of 0 or more.
datasources.form.unknownKind: This kind of data source is not available on this server.
datasources.secret.hint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
datasources.secret.replaceHint: Replaces the stored value when you save. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
datasources.delete.title: Delete data source?
datasources.delete.text: “{name}” moves to the trash. Panels that query it show an error until it is restored.
datasources.settings.path: Absolute path of the database file
datasources.editor.label: Query
datasources.editor.shortcuts: Ctrl+Enter runs the query, Ctrl+Space shows suggestions.
datasources.editor.schemaFailed: The schema could not be loaded, so suggestions cover keywords only.
datasources.editor.unsupported: There is no query editor for this kind of data source yet.
datasources.editor.macrosLead: Macros take the dashboard time range. Kalzit passes them as parameters, never as text in the query.
datasources.editor.macro.timeFilter: True for rows whose column lies in the time range.
datasources.editor.macro.interval: Suggested grouping interval for the time range, such as 1m.
datasources.editor.instant: Instant query: one value per series at the end of the time range
datasources.editor.kind.label: label
datasources.form.nameTaken: Another data source already has this name. Choose a different one.
datasources.trash.title: Data source trash
datasources.trash.lead: Deleted data sources stay here. Restore one to use it again in Explore and dashboards.
datasources.editor.sqlHint: One SELECT or WITH statement. Variables are written $name and reach the database as parameters.
datasources.editor.promHint: Variables only inside quoted strings, such as job=“$job”.
datasources.editor.minStepInvalid: Enter a number of seconds, such as 15.
datasources.editor.promMacrosLead: Macros take the time range of the dashboard or of Explore.
datasources.editor.macro.rateInterval: Four intervals, at least 1m: a safe window for rate().
datasources.editor.macro.range: The length of the time range.
datasources.editor.macro.timeFromSeconds: Start of the time range in Unix seconds.
datasources.editor.macro.timeToSeconds: End of the time range in Unix seconds.
datasources.settings.trustServerCertific: Trust the server certificate without checking it (only for tests)
datasources.settings.hosts: Hosts (host or host:port, separated by commas)
datasources.settings.srv: Look up the servers in DNS (mongodb+srv)
datasources.kinds.postgres.hint: Use a login that can only read, for example a role with only SELECT rights such as a member of pg_read_all_data. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.kinds.mysql.hint: Use a user with only the SELECT privilege on the databases you need. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.kinds.mssql.hint: Use a login in the db_datareader role only. Kalzit rejects queries that change data, but a read-only login is the real protection.
datasources.kinds.sqlite.hint: Kalzit opens SQLite files read-only, and only from folders a server admin allowed.
datasources.kinds.prometheus.hint: Use credentials that can only read, if your server needs any.
datasources.kinds.mongodb.hint: Use a login with only the read role on this database. Kalzit refuses logins that may do more, and servers without access control.
datasources.secret.reenter: The connection target changed, so enter this again (or remove it) before saving. Kalzit never sends a stored secret to a new target unasked.
datasources.form.readOnlyAccess: You may use this data source but not change it. An admin can give you edit access.
datasources.form.targetLocked: You may change the name, limits and secrets. Where the source connects (host, port, user, TLS, URL or path) only a data source admin can change.
datasources.reason.request.body_invalid: The request was not in the expected form: {detail}
datasources.reason.request.query_invalid: The list request has parameters the server does not know: {detail}
datasources.reason.request.limit: Ask for 1 to {max} entries at a time.
datasources.reason.request.trash: The trash filter must be true or false.
datasources.reason.request.cursor: This page of the list is no longer valid. Load the list again.

datasources.reason.settings.not_object: The settings could not be read.
datasources.reason.settings.unknown: “{name}” is no setting of this kind of data source.
datasources.reason.settings.secret_in_se: “{field}” is a secret and belongs in the secret fields.
datasources.reason.settings.expected_num: Enter a whole number of at least 0.
datasources.reason.settings.control_char: The value may not contain control characters such as line breaks.

datasources.reason.settings.host_invalid: Enter a host name or an IP address.
datasources.reason.settings.pem_invalid: Paste a CA certificate in PEM form (-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----).
datasources.reason.settings.path_relativ: Enter the full path of the file, starting at the drive or at /.
datasources.reason.settings.url_scheme: The URL must start with http:// or https://.
datasources.reason.settings.url_credenti: Leave user name and password out of the URL; use the secret fields.
datasources.reason.settings.url_query: The URL may not contain a query string (?) or a fragment (#).
datasources.reason.settings.invalid: These settings do not fit this kind of data source: {detail}
datasources.reason.secrets.unknown: “{name}” is no secret of this kind of data source.
datasources.reason.secrets.resend_on_tar: “{field}” changes where the data source connects. Enter “{secret}” again, or remove it, so a stored secret never goes to a new target unasked.
datasources.reason.target.sqlite_path_re: Kalzit may not open this file. It has to exist, lie in a folder the server admin allowed for SQLite, outside Kalzit's own data folder, and be on a local drive.

datasources.reason.target.metadata_addre: Kalzit does not connect to {host}: it is a link-local or cloud metadata address.
datasources.reason.target.not_allowed: The server admin has not allowed connections to {host}.
datasources.reason.target.scheme_not_all: Kalzit connects only over http or https, not {scheme}.
datasources.reason.target.own_database: This is Kalzit's own database; it cannot be a data source.
datasources.reason.target.own_database_u: Kalzit cannot check that this server is not its own database, so it does not connect.
datasources.reason.target.unresolvable: The host name {host} could not be resolved: {detail}
datasources.reason.target.unreachable: No address of {host} accepted a connection: {detail}
datasources.reason.query.invalid_form: The query does not fit this data source: {detail}
datasources.reason.query.count: Send 1 to {max} queries at a time.
datasources.reason.query.ref_id: Every query needs its own short name (at most 64 characters).
datasources.reason.query.range_out_of_bo: The time range has to lie between the years 1 and 9999.
datasources.reason.query.range_reversed: The start of the time range is after its end.
datasources.reason.query.interval_out_of: The interval has to be between 1 ms and one year.
datasources.reason.query.time_out_of_ran: The database cannot hold the time {time}.
datasources.reason.query.write_refused: Kalzit only reads; the database refused a change: {detail}
datasources.reason.query.timeout: The query ran longer than {seconds} s and was stopped.
datasources.reason.query.statement_timeo: PostgreSQL stopped the query at its statement timeout.
datasources.reason.sql.multiple_statemen: Send one statement at a time.
datasources.reason.sql.not_select: Only SELECT and WITH are allowed; Kalzit only reads.
datasources.reason.sql.select_into: SELECT INTO writes data, which Kalzit does not do.
datasources.reason.sql.locking_clause: Locking clauses such as FOR UPDATE are not allowed.
datasources.reason.sql.function_not_allo: The function {name} is not allowed: it reaches files, the network or the session.
datasources.reason.sql.sequence: NEXT VALUE FOR changes a sequence and is not allowed.
datasources.reason.sql.table_hint: The table hint {hint} is not allowed; only NOLOCK and READUNCOMMITTED are.
datasources.reason.sql.legacy_table_hint: Write the table hint of {alias} as WITH (…).
datasources.reason.sql.executable_commen: MySQL comments of the form /*!…*/ are not allowed.
datasources.reason.sql.dash_comment_spac: Put an ordinary space after -- in a comment.
datasources.reason.sql.placeholder: Use variables ($name) instead of placeholders like $1, ? or :name.
datasources.reason.sql.parse_error: Kalzit could not read the statement to check it: {detail}
datasources.reason.sql.variable_format_u: The format :{format} is unknown; only :identifier exists.
datasources.reason.sql.variable_type: The value of {name} must be text, a number, true, false or a list of them.
datasources.reason.sql.identifier_variab: Only constant and custom variables may name tables or columns; {name} is neither.
datasources.reason.sql.identifier_unknow: The value of {name} is no table or column of this data source.
datasources.reason.sql.identifier_needs_: Variables that name tables or columns need the schema of the data source, which could not be read.
datasources.reason.promql.variable_outsi: Put the variable {name} inside a quoted label value, such as job=“${name}”.
datasources.reason.promql.variable_type: The value of {name} must be text, a number, true, false or a list of them.
datasources.reason.promql.backtick: The value of {name} contains a backtick, which a raw string cannot hold.
datasources.reason.variables.too_many: A dashboard has at most {max} variables.
datasources.reason.variables.too_large: The variable values are too large together (at most {bytes} bytes).
datasources.reason.variables.unknown: The saved dashboard has no variable {name}. Save the dashboard first.
datasources.reason.variables.constant: {name} is a constant; its value cannot be chosen.
datasources.reason.variables.not_an_opti: “{value}” is not one of the values of {name}.
datasources.reason.variables.value_type: The value of {name} must be a value or a list of values.
datasources.reason.variables.self_depend: The options of {name} cannot depend on {name} itself.
datasources.reason.variables.not_a_query: {name} takes its values from no query.
datasources.reason.variables.not_a_frame: The variable's query has to answer a table.
datasources.reason.source.error: The data source reported an error: {detail}
datasources.reason.source.no_answer: The data source sent no answer.
datasources.reason.sqlite.open_failed: The SQLite file could not be opened: {detail}
datasources.reason.mysql.no_time_limit: This MySQL or MariaDB server cannot limit the run time of a query, so Kalzit does not query it.
datasources.reason.mssql.login_timeout: SQL Server did not complete the sign-in in time.
datasources.reason.prometheus.credential: The credentials contain characters an HTTP header cannot carry.
datasources.reason.prometheus.not_an_api: The server answered (HTTP {status}), but not like a Prometheus API. Check the URL.
datasources.reason.prometheus.result_typ: Prometheus answered with a result type Kalzit does not show ({type}).
datasources.reason.http.timeout: The data source did not answer in time.
datasources.reason.http.too_large: The answer was larger than {bytes} bytes.
datasources.reason.http.failed: The request to the data source failed: {detail}
datasources.reason.secrets.unreadable: The secrets of this data source cannot be read. Enter them again.
datasources.reason.secrets.undecryptable: The stored “{field}” cannot be decrypted, likely because the secrets key changed. Enter it again.
datasources.reason.settings.stored_inval: The stored settings no longer fit this kind of data source. Open it and save it again.
datasources.reason.server.shutting_down: The server is shutting down. Try again in a moment.
datasources.reason.internal: Something went wrong on the server. The server log has the details.
datasources.reason.health.connected_admi: Connected to {engine} {version}, but the login has administrator rights. Use a read-only login.
datasources.reason.health.connected_read: Connected to {engine} {version}; the file is opened read-only.
datasources.reason.frame.row_limit: The result was cut at {rows} rows.
datasources.reason.frame.size_limit: The result was cut at the size limit of an answer.
datasources.reason.frame.binary_hidden: Binary values of {column} are not shown.
datasources.reason.frame.type_unsupporte: Kalzit cannot show the type {type} of {column}.
datasources.reason.frame.value_mismatch: {count} values of {column} do not fit its type and are left empty.
datasources.form.atLeast: Enter a value of at least {min}.
datasources.settings.allowWriteCapableUs: Allow a user that may write (only the query check protects the data)
datasources.settings.approvedQueries: Approved installed queries (names, separated by commas or line breaks)
datasources.kinds.neo4j.hint: Use a user with only read rights (the reader role). Kalzit also runs every query in a read transaction, which Neo4j enforces.
datasources.kinds.memgraph.hint: Use a user that may only read. Memgraph does not enforce read transactions, so Kalzit checks the user and refuses one that may write, unless you allow it (needed for Memgraph Community).
datasources.kinds.tigergraph.hint: Use a user with only the queryreader role. Kalzit checks the user's rights and refuses one that may write, and checks the text of every query.
datasources.reason.settings.name_invalid: Use only letters, digits and _ here (user names also - . @).
datasources.reason.cypher.multiple_state: Send one statement at a time.
datasources.reason.cypher.not_read_query: A query has to start with MATCH, OPTIONAL MATCH, WITH, UNWIND, RETURN or CALL; Kalzit only reads.
datasources.reason.cypher.foreach: FOREACH can only change data and is not allowed.
datasources.reason.cypher.load: LOAD reads files or URLs on the server and is not allowed.
datasources.reason.cypher.use: USE is not allowed; the data source's settings choose the database.
datasources.reason.cypher.in_transaction: Writing in batches (IN TRANSACTIONS, PERIODIC COMMIT) is not allowed.
datasources.reason.cypher.procedure_not_: The procedure {name} is not on the list of read procedures.
datasources.reason.cypher.parse_error: CALL needs a procedure name or a subquery.
datasources.reason.cypher.variable_type: The value of {name} must be text, a number, true, false or a list of them.
datasources.reason.gsql.not_one_query: Send exactly one query of the form INTERPRET QUERY (parameters) FOR GRAPH name { body }.
datasources.reason.gsql.parse_error: Kalzit could not read the query to check it: {detail}
datasources.reason.gsql.attribute_assign: Assigning an attribute ({target}) changes data; Kalzit only reads.
datasources.reason.gsql.file_output: Writing files (TO_CSV, FILE) is not allowed.
datasources.reason.gsql.statement_not_al: {statement} is not allowed in a query Kalzit runs.
datasources.reason.gsql.function_not_all: {name} is not a built-in function Kalzit allows. Calls of other queries are not allowed either.
datasources.reason.gsql.other_graph: The query is for the graph {graph}, not for the graph of this data source.
datasources.reason.gsql.string_escape: A backslash before a quote is not allowed inside a string; whether it ends the string depends on the TigerGraph version.
datasources.reason.gsql.unexpected_chara: The character {character} is not allowed outside strings and comments.
datasources.reason.tigergraph.query_text: Kalzit cannot read the text of {name} to check it. A data source admin can approve the query by name.

datasources.reason.bolt.login_timeout: The server did not complete the sign-in in time.
datasources.reason.bolt.too_large: A single answer of the server was larger than the size limit.
datasources.reason.memgraph.user_can_wri: The Memgraph user has rights beyond reading ({privileges}): changing data, reading files on the server, or managing users, triggers, streams or settings. Use a user that may only read, or allow such a user in the settings.

datasources.reason.tigergraph.credential: The credentials contain characters an HTTP header cannot carry.
datasources.reason.tigergraph.not_an_api: The server answered (HTTP {status}), but not like TigerGraph. Check the URL.
datasources.reason.health.connected_writ: Connected to {engine} {version}, but the user may change data ({privileges}). Only Kalzit's query check keeps queries read-only.
